hook: SCP-2020 is a lanky, bright green alien made of rubber that lives on shredded paper and badly wants to become a science fiction writer. Nearly the whole article is one monologue it delivers to a researcher, and its charm is the rhythm: excited, scattered, always interrupting itself for a better idea. Keep an ear on the stock phrase it tacks onto almost every pitch.
whyItMatters: The clinical part of the file is brief, covering an unusual body and an origin story the entity changes every time it is asked. The real subject is a character: harmless, indifferent to its cell, and unable to write a single line because it cannot settle on one concept. The object class, Euclid-exsequi, is listed without any explanation, which leaves that label as one more small oddity.
thingsToNotice: The pitches run through a world-restoring facility, a brain in a jar who becomes a superhero, a cyborg space wizard with five cyborg catgirls fighting space crime, a simulation AI that eats brains, and a time machine crew trying to secure an asteroid apocalypse, and each one gets called cliche by the alien itself. The sixth idea is about an alien exactly like it, talking to a government agency that already possesses everything it describes while the agents wonder whether it knows any of it is real. The article never confirms that reading, but the procedure requiring every word in the cell to be transcribed, and a recovery file with Roswell in its name, look different once you have heard it. The monologue ends with a pitch it announces as two words, delivers as three, and then concedes that this is harder than it expected.
